season.name: Summer
season.line: Labor without Sabbath becomes bondage, however fruitful it looks.

movement.name: The Long Day
movement.line: Endurance is the work of wisdom.

days.t: Run with endurance the race set before us
x: Therefore we also, having such a great cloud of witnesses encompassing us, having put off every weight and the sin easily entangling, should run through perseverance the race lying before us,

looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of [our] faith, who in view of the joy lying before Him endured the cross, having despised [its] shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

days.t: Run so as to obtain the prize
x: Do you⁺ not know that those running in a race indeed all run, but one receives the prize? Run thus, so that you⁺ might obtain [it].
Now everyone striving controls himself in all things; these indeed then so that they might receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable.
Brothers, I do not reckon myself to have taken hold [of it]. But one thing: Indeed, forgetting the things behind and stretching forward to the things ahead,
I pursue toward the goal for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.

days.t: The soldier, the athlete, the farmer
x: Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one serving as a soldier entangles himself in the affairs of life, so that he might please the one having enlisted him.
Now also, if anyone competes, he is not crowned unless he shall have competed lawfully.
It is necessary for the toiling farmer first to partake of the fruits.

days.t: They go from strength to strength
x: Blessed is the man whose help is of thee, O Lord; in his heart he has purposed to go up
the valley of weeping, to the place which he has appointed, for [there] the law-giver will grant blessings.
They shall go from strength to strength: the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith.
